subject: Channel partner onboarding — gap analysis & entitlement mapping exception
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@cloudbridge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace onboarding — entitlement mapping questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We started filling out the onboarding checklist and ran into a couple of blockers that will affect our go-live window. Two quick items:

1) Entitlement mapping: our ISV product IDs are hierarchical (suite > module > feature). The marketplace import expects a flat SKU per listing. We need either an exception for multi-tier mappings or guidance on an automated transform.

2) Billing hooks: we currently handle metered usage via our billing provider and want Redwood to surface usage events via webhook. Are there constraints about event frequency or signature verification we should know about?

I've attached the onboarding_checklist.xlsx with highlighted rows. Can we get product + billing engineering eyes on this?

Goal: decide by EOD Thu (4/5) whether we can onboard on Redwood Marketplace in our May release or if we need the alternate flow (direct marketplace listing + manual entitlement sync).

Appreciate the help — happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Partnerships, CloudBridge Solutions

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace onboarding — entitlement mapping questions

Thanks Sarah — looping in product and integrations.

Karthik / Marissa: please see the attached checklist from CloudBridge. Two asks:
- Can the marketplace import accept a CSV with parent_id/child_id columns and materialize multiple entitlement rows on our side (preferred)? If not, what would the least-effort transform look like?
- Billing webhooks: CloudBridge is asking about rate limits and signatures. We have a 1,000 req/min per tenant guideline for webhooks; signature is HMAC-SHA256 using the tenant secret. Any edge cases?

Karthik — can you triage feasibility and estimate dev work (rough T-shirt)? Marissa — any UI/partner console implications for mapping exceptions?

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Partner Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace onboarding — entitlement mapping questions

Vanessa / team — quick read:

Entitlement mapping:
- Our import pipeline currently expects one SKU per listing row, but the ingestion service is flexible. We can accept parent_id/child_id and expand into N entitlements during import. Work estimate: ~3-4 dev days + 1 day QA to add transform + update schema validation. Risk: existing partners who relied on flat SKUs may need a migration plan.

Billing webhooks:
- Rate limit: 1,000 req/min/tenant (we can raise per partner with an SLA).
- Signature: HMAC-SHA256, include timestamp header (we already verify 5m window).
- Implementation notes: we'll add a partner toggle to opt-in to high-frequency events to avoid noisy default. Dev estimate: 2 days to expose toggle + docs update.

I recommend we do an onboarding exception for CloudBridge: accept hierarchical mapping for their initial listing, ship the import transform, and then schedule a follow-up to standardize mapping (Q2).

I'll draft a short mutual action plan if we agree.

-karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -07:00

Forwarded message below for context.

> Thanks Sarah — looping in product and integrations.
> 
> Karthik / Marissa: please see the attached checklist from CloudBridge. Two asks:
> - Can the marketplace import accept a CSV with parent_id/child_id columns and materialize multiple entitlement rows on our side (preferred)? If not, what would the least-effort transform look like?
> - Billing webhooks: CloudBridge is asking about rate limits and signatures. We have a 1,000 req/min per tenant guideline for webhooks; signature is HMAC-SHA256 using the tenant secret. Any edge cases?

Adding a couple of operational notes:
- Partner console: if we grant an exception, we should create a temporary "mapping profile" record for CloudBridge so that the Marketplace UI shows the owner and prevents accidental edits. That's a small schema + UI flag change (1 dev day).
- Compliance: because mapping changes touch entitlement resolution, we should capture a short audit log entry (basic DB write) for the initial exception + eventual migration. This is low-effort but important for Dedicated/private customers later.
- Timeline: if we start the transform this week, we can complete work and run a dry import by Fri 4/5; production list could go live the week of 4/15 if procurement signs by then.

I'll add a short runbook for the import and share the draft in Drive (link below).

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

Drive draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-onboarding-templates

- Karthik: implement import transform + add validation (ETA: 4/5 EOD)

- Contracts (CloudBridge): sign standard MSLA + PO and return (ETA: 4/12)

If all goes to plan we target live listing week of 4/15. If procurement slips, we will fall back to manual entitlement sync.

I'll set up the go/no-go calendar invite for Fri 4/13 10am PT and share the Drive folder.

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Vanessa Ortiz | Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
